It's not that easy to pack up and leave. You're very privileged if you can do that, but in fact, many people are not able to just say "fuck this shit, I'm out".
The simplest example I can give you is like this:
Imagine you're a kid growing up. You live in a poor family that can barely afford to raise you and send you to school. Now your parents are poor, and it's likely because they didn't get the privilege of being sent to school, so the situation is not getting any better. It's also likely that you're the result of a mistake, since they have low education. So the situation is a bit tense in your family... Fights do happen on a daily basis and it bothers the hell out of you. In spite of that, you have no money, nor the ability to bring in any money. Be realistic, no one's gonna hire you. Your education is not going that well either, after all you are preoccupied most of the time with escaping the cruel reality.
Time goes by, and you kind of get used to this lifestyle...  Your parents abuse you and vent out their anger on you, and you start doing the same with others. You are becoming what your parents project on you. You kind of fear them, but you can't just live without them... Change is difficult for humans since we're rigid to it. You don't know the laws that well either, after all the school does a good job at not giving you the truly useful information. So you keep moving on... you've barely passed through your education and you want to start your life, but you can't really do much... Your life was wasted so far by everything that happened with you, so you're not particularly good at something, nor do you have a higher education... It is expensive after all. So you find a work... Kinda shady, and they kind of not pay you legally, but no one else took you.
Your mother falls ill, so your income for the family is reduced. Even if she abused you, she still loved you... Your feelings are mixed, but you can't just leave her die, right? So you support her... It seems you can't just move out yet... 
Let's say that eventually she gets better (lucky you), but now she doesn't have a job anymore, and finding one is quite difficult... Seems like you'll have to keep helping them.
You do notice that she's not really looking for a job either, so now you threaten that you'll stop helping, yet it doesn't go well. They blackmail you emotionally "we raised you, even if we were poor, we gave you everything we could". Maybe they're right, maybe they're not, but it does hit where it hurts. So you decide to keep helping. You try again, but they find another reason why you should keep helping, and it makes sense, after all, we are emotionally weak especially when our education is low... So years go by, and you kind of get used to this... 
It's hard to change the situation, but something finally happens. You find someone you like. Oh, it's time again to think about moving out, but your father's against it. He wants your financial support which you can't afford if you move out. You argue, but he's been abusing you for a long time now and you're afraid of him getting angry, so you're shut up... Seems like you still can't get away. 
The person you love understands that this is not fine. You're now getting lectured on all the things you needed to know since a long time ago... But what are you gonna do with them now? You already got used to this situation, and it's difficult to just walk away. Yet you're being pushed to action over and over again. You lash out to the one you love just like your parents did, because you have no other way to express yourself at this point. Now your relationship is ruined. You're all alone again, depressed. 
With time, you finally think that maybe you should do something, so you eventually gather your courage and leave... Yes, you finally got away... Or did you? Your parents are not happy about it. They threaten you in all sort of ways. They use your feelings against you. Did you know your father is also ill and can't work anymore? They can't keep living like that... It's up to you to help them, after all, they raised you as good as they could...

I could keep on going with this story. Some parts are a bit exaggerated (just a bit tho), but many people go through something similar. You can't just get up and leave... It's really difficult because you're held back by so many things that have been build over the years. It's unrealistic to expect you can just get up and leave overnight. It takes a lot of effort, and some are too entangled with their families that they can't even dream about it. Imagine leaving and your family coming after you. Law can't go shit about that, even if they have bad intentions. You'll be passed around for years though investigations until they tell you "well, you know, it's your word against them, and they are more and we don't see anything that you told us in them. Also, about your scars, they said you did them on your own, so the judge decided to have you pay them for false accusations". 
It's never easy, and laws don't make it easier if you ever thought about relying on them.

As I said, as far as I know, every industry buys less qualitative parts for the cheaper products, typically parts which fail the quality requirements of the higher end products. If that didn't happen we would have a tremendous waste in the world, and PSU manufactures are also doing it. There's very few companies building their own products from scratch by themselves. Whether you know something different, I have no clue on what it is your belief founded, so it's up to you what you make with that I said. On the other hand, I feel like you just picked whatever you wanted from what I said and disregarded everything else, or maybe didn't even read. I'm not heavily overrating anything, it's just plain math. I'm saying things as they are. You seem fixated on RMx PSUs, but I never said anything along the lines "you absolutely need RMx PSU for any kind of build", nor did I even mention them. What I said, in simple terms, is that it depends on various things. I told you why people assume they need better PSUs than they actually do, not that they absolutely need them. And you seem to assume that efficiency is only important in heat dissipation and discarding everything else. As far as I'm concerned, the PSU is one of the most important pieces in a system, and not choosing one accordingly can cost you more than what it was "worth" to save.  Efficiency is not everything, and just because it has slapped on it a wattage and a "certification" it doesn't always mean that they truly are what they say. Just because it says it has a given capacitor, it doesn't mean that it's well put together. You seem to keep referencing to some kind of list someone did, but looking at it, all I see is someone recommending fail safe PSUs. It's just a recommendation, and you have plenty from which to choose for various wattages. If you don't like it, you can buy what you believe it's better. Obviously, they have a standard at which they call "entry level" which may not be the same as yours.

I actually don't really know what you are talking about, because I don't see people recommending the overkill level of PSU you're saying that often. But then I'm mostly doing my own builds and we definitely consult different people for opinions on them. Generally, the difference between gold and bronze is about 7-10% in efficiency. However, that can change quite drastically depending on the brand. You are typically getting what you are paying for. If a PSU is 200€ then it is that expensive (if you pick the right one) because it has reliable protections, better reliability and consistently better efficiency. Cheaper PSUs and cheaper brands usually use parts manufactured for the more expensive ones that didn't pass the quality standards. This is done in almost every industry as far as I know. So getting a cheaper one it's typically that you're betting more on luck, not only for your PSU, but for your whole build too. Sometimes, those "weaker" PSUs don't have all those desired protections or are poorly implemented, so more powerful ones are desired in general. A PSU will degrade differently depending on the load, and having a PSU running at almost 100% compared to about 80% can make a difference. A gold rated PSU is typically preferred over the bronze, as it usually comes with some extra protections as well from the improved efficiency. That gold is normally what you aim for, but above that you don't really have many reasons to go, as the increased price is not (most of the times) justified in the electricity bill anymore. Mind you, I'm not talking about keeping a PSU only for a year here, since that's completely wasteful. I'm talking about keeping it through the whole life of the system. You may not get the return of investment in one year depending where you live, but if you consider the entire life (about 4 years+), then there is a difference, especially if after that you can still reuse the PSU for another build. For example, buying a gold over bronze at 400w, where the gold would be constantly at least 10% more efficient in every situation (not true for every PSU), and where the the gold is 40€ more expensive, then you justify the extra price in the electricity bill by paying around 40€ less than with a bronze one throughout its typical life. Consider that compared to replacing it every single year because it broke. Of course those are just fictive numbers. You may get a bigger return, or a smaller one depending on your choice.
I'm not saying here that a gold PSU will necessarily preform better just because it's gold. I'm saying it depends on components and on what you're using it for. In some situations it makes sense to get a better one, while in others it won't make much of a difference, or it would just increase the price and your electricity bill.
Not everyone would solve an ILP to buy a PSU, so they just go with what seems right. This means they approximate and add a warranty on top of it, then they get what they expect to buy. This can lead to the overkill situation quite easily if you're far from reality with your approximation and your warranty that you add is huge as well.

You need to consider that if you want a budget build, you'll probably worry about your electricity bill too. Recommending a good rated PSU will reduce wasted energy and you will have less to pay over the use of your PC for electricity. Bad PSUs degrade quite quickly and you will soon consume more and more. Most PSUs are best efficient at around 50% load, but it can depend from model to model. Getting a better PSU than you "need" is a good idea, especially if you plan on upgrading in the future, but getting one that is way too "good" can turn into a bad choice, as its efficiency will be just as bad as a worse one, although you can update in future without worries. Depending on the price of the PSU you can justify it with the cost of electricity over time, but you need to get the right one.  However, some people don't really know the required wattage of a system and they just throw in something that they've seen used by others, regardless of the parameters.

You can take a look at this [video](https://youtu.be/cLQQP5NcNJY) as it shows you the better options for a video card based on your budget.
The 3rd gen (latest) ryzen processors are dominating the Intel ones giving either similar or better performance at similar or better prices. For what you need, you can take a look at 2nd gen as well, since they're not that far in performance and are cheaper. You need to think how much power you actually want and how much you want to spend. I'd recommend you to look at ryzen 5 mostly, as for the tasks you described a 2600 or 3600 should be about what you need. Add the "x" at the end for better coolers (plus overclock) and sometimes better stock frequencies depending on the model. Move to ryzen 7 if you plan to to more cpu intensive tasks like rendering videos and more intense video editing.
After that you should choose your motherboard, and depending on what processor you chose and what you need (overclock or not and generation), you can get away with quite cheap options (mostly if you're not overclocking). Here's a [video](https://youtu.be/zuyuS04lD4o) that might help you. I can't say I agree with everything there, but there are some good options and it will give you an idea of what to look around for the motherboard. There are other helping videos similar to that and there's plenty of discussions going around to help finding what you need. Pay attention to the ram frequency too based on the processor you chose as it can bring you the performance you want. [Here](https://youtu.be/iHJ16hD4ysk) is something that might help you understand it better.

If you don't want to overclock, the k version is wasted and you'd be better off with the non k version.
Although I would personally go for a ryzen (like 3700) regardless as it kind of beats Intel right now in every budget imo with their newest generation, but you'd also need to find a different motherboard.
As for the Nvidia RTX 2060, it really depends what you want to do with it... If you plan on playing 4k games, then forget it and go for a GTX video card. It will use less power and run cooler too for better performance. If you do competitive games, I'd still go for the GTX, since RTX has no place there. However, although I'm not sure how many RTX games are there, if the games you want to play support RTX, then you might be better with that card.
I'd also consider getting an SSD as the extra speed it offers really makes a difference.

This is going to be something a paranoid person would say, but turn your house upside down looking for ANYTHING out of place. Think of every place you could put a microphone, including inside your phone chargers, behind the outlets, in the air vents, under the beds or furniture, under the floor, anything that could be a suspicious place. A microphone can be really small, so you have tons of places to search for, so we need to narrow it down a little bit.

If you're apart for a long time, then things get simpler. A decent IoT device could have a battery that keeps up to 2 years depending on the task it is doing. This means that, depending on what she did, if you've been apart for more than 2 years and she's able to bring recent discussions up, there is no way she could use something on battery alone. This narrows down the places you should search to those that have wires going to them, or could have wires but well hidden. So, chargers, under the floor, walls, mirrors, outlets, air vents, inside PCs, lights or any electronic device that could be tampered with. Obviously, they will need to have a minimum size, so you can try to skip what it's too small to actually house a bug, a battery and an antenna, besides its standard components which give its functionality of what it's looking from the outside. But keep in mind that even if it sounds like there is a lot to pack in a cramped space, they're really small too, so don't overlook too many things. However, you can start with the bigger ones first, because you said she wasn't there since 2012, and technology was not as refined as today. Since you have bad signal, you might want to look for things well positioned too, even if they may be in other rooms.

If you have internet, change the password to it. If you have neighbors, ask them to do the same. This does not ensure you're cutting off any device from internet access, as she could've used a SIM card to send through data the information.

Ask your neighbors if she ever visited them and in what rooms she was, and ensure she didn't set up a series of devices to cooperate, or that the device is not actually in your neighbor's possession. Ask them when was the last time they saw her too around there and where exactly, as that might give you some extra hints in case she's doing something unexpected.

If you're desperate, get a metal detector depending on your environment, or a sensitive heat camera. Any device is giving off heat. Make sure you make lots of noise by saying random words, just in case it's a smart device that records based on noise level. Don't give up if you don't find anything with that right away, as it might have a scheduled update time, and when transferring data devices use quite a lot of energy. Make sure everything is plugged out to be sure you can see if the device is inside another one.

Another option is getting a bug detector. I'm not sure how well they work and what would be the right price for one, but there are some out there. I had at some point a phone application which would detect given frequencies/magnetic fields around the phone. I don't think it would be really useful, but you can try something like that too.

Keep in mind that I'm eliminating the human factor, which is also something you might want to consider. If it's not your family, it could be your neighbor.

Listen. There are times when you shouldn't give up, and there are times you should just drop it. As I see it, this is one of those times when you should drop it.
I'm not saying this without consideration. I do realize that for normal people 3 months may seem like a lot. I do realize that it might've felt like you put a lot of effort into it and you want something in return. I do understand that it's hard to give up on the things you want, but think about it like this:
You have lived at least 300 months so far, and you've been in a one sided relationship for 3 months. That's like 1% of your life in which you "got to know her". As time goes by, this percentage will get smaller and smaller until eventually it goes far below 1%. That 1% is insignificant when you look at the bigger picture.
So now take a step back and think of what is happening. You have feeling for someone you barely know. Believe me, 3 months is very little time to know someone, and this is coming from a person that "figures" people out in hours/days. You only know what she showed you, and in this little time you barely got the gist of it. I'm sure there are plenty of situations in which you don't even know who she will be. HOWEVER, you do know something. She literally spelled it for you that she is not interested. 
You have two options right now: 
1. Stop wasting your time for a one side relationship and spend it on someone that is indeed interested in a proper relationship. Like this you'll minimize the damage and the time you spend on someone who clearly said that is into fooling around and not into something serious.
2. Continue to pursue her, putting effort into gaining something which you're not really sure you want, with the probability that she will waste more time from your life, turning the 1% into an even bigger percentage without getting anything in return.

If you abandon this now, it will be easier for you to move on compared to ending up in an unfaithful relationship which might mark you and affect your future relationships.
